subtype: Approach: working backward from a target role [Thinking]
passage:
I sit next to Devika, and last month I watched Devika try to plan the next five years. Devika wants to be a software architect before thirty. On a big sheet taped to the wall, in three columns, went what that job needs: designing whole systems, leading a team, and knowing one field really well.
Then came the years. Year one: system design, with a course and one design document a quarter. Year two: lead a small team on a project. Year three: go deep on one business area. Later years were pencilled in lightly.
Devika stepped back and said, "Okay." I couldn't tell if that meant excited or scared. Probably both.
— Swati

qa.q: What three things did Devika list as needed for the job?
qa.a: Devika listed designing whole systems, leading a team and knowing one field well.

qa.q: What might Devika have been feeling when stepping back from the sheet and saying "Okay"?
qa.a: Devika might have felt excited and scared at once, though Swati cannot tell which.

qa.q: What could Devika do if year one's course turns out weaker than expected?
qa.a: Devika could swap it for another way to learn design, such as a design review with a senior colleague, and keep the yearly slot.

qa.q: What is it like for Swati to watch Devika plan?
qa.a: Swati feels curious and a little impressed, and also uncertain about what Devika feels.

grounding: The account shows a developer aiming to become an architect who lists what the role needs and assigns each item to a year.
